MER00049MT.text:
Production Planning at Mercedes-Benz designs and industrializes the production systems required for future vehicle architectures. Its responsibilities span factory, logistics, body, paint and assembly planning. Teams coordinate changing vehicle requirements, production scenarios, investment decisions and planning results across multiple engineering disciplines and IT applications. The Engineering Version Management System, eVMS, supports this work through the concept of versioned planning. The eVMS structures planning baselines, alternative scenarios, check requests and shop-specific results. It provides traceable links between decisions, premises and engineering documents while leaving detailed planning work in the established specialist applications. Currently, we are in a phase of transitioning from software testing into operational rollout. At the same time, the project is extending the platform with AI-supported workflows, an internal agent, system connectors and integration with the broader engineering toolchain.
Your Internship
As an intern in the eVMS project, you will work at the intersection of production planning, digital product management, software development and applied artificial intelligence.
You will help introduce eVMS into operational planning processes, shape the internal eVMS agent and translate user needs into structured requirements for the development team. This is not a purely administrative rollout role. You will work directly with users, developers and technical experts and contribute tangible improvements to the product.
Tasks and Responsibilities
Support the eVMS rollout:
Support the preparation and execution of rollout activities with production-planning projects and specialist departments
Help onboard key users and guide them through the versioned-planning methodology and the eVMS application
Prepare concise training materials, demonstrations, user guides and rollout communications
Facilitate testing sessions, interviews and feedback workshops with project managers, shop project leads and production-planning engineers
Document user feedback, usability issues, process gaps and rollout dependencies in a structured format
Support the definition of adoption indicators and evaluate how eVMS affects user experience, traceability and planning coordination
Help establish a scalable rollout approach that can be transferred to further projects, plants and planning units
The current rollout approach deliberately combines practical user testing with structured feedback so that unclear functions and usability problems can be identified and transferred into product improvements.
Guide the development of the internal eVMS agent:
Analyze user activities that could be supported or automated through the internal eVMS agent
Collect and structure use cases for AI-supported planning, such as summarizing changes, preparing version information, identifying conflicts or creating structured planning entries
Define expected agent behavior, required context, user interactions and human approval points
Support the design of prompts, knowledge sources and contextual information required by the agent
Test agent responses and workflows against realistic production-planning scenarios
Evaluate output quality, usability, traceability and potential failure cases
Work with technical experts on agent integration through APIs, webhooks, workflows and the Model Context Protocol
Help ensure that sensitive or consequential actions remain transparent and subject to appropriate human approval
The existing eVMS direction combines a git-like approach with event-driven n8n workflows, contextual payloads, MCP-based access to connected applications and human approval for non-read actions.
Shape software development through user requirements:
Observe and analyze current production-planning workflows, decision points and information handovers
Translate user demands into clear problem statements, user stories and functional requirements
Formulate acceptance criteria and realistic test scenarios for new eVMS features
Structure and prioritize requirements together with the product owner and development team
Clarify requirements with users and developers throughout implementation
Support sprint preparation, feature reviews and validation of completed software increments
Test new functions in the development and production environments and document defects in a reproducible manner
Contribute ideas for UI and UX improvements, system connectors and workflow automation
Help maintain alignment between user needs, the versioned-planning methodology and the technical implementation
The eVMS project already uses Scrum-based development, Jira work items, user stories, acceptance criteria and iterative testing to connect production-planning requirements with implementation.
Work across business and technology:
Collaborate with production planners, project-management roles, the eVMS product team and software developers
Support communication between German business stakeholders and the distributed development team
Prepare decision material, feature descriptions and development priorities for project discussions
Research relevant approaches in agentic AI, workflow automation, knowledge graphs and engineering software
Document implementation concepts, test findings and lessons learned in a form that can be reused by the project
Your internship can start from 1st of January 2027.
What you can expect:
Direct involvement in the rollout of a digital product within Mercedes-Benz production planning
A role combining user interaction, product management, AI engineering and software development
The opportunity to shape real product requirements rather than work on an isolated academic exercise
Practical experience with an international and interdisciplinary development setup
Exposure to versioned planning, AI-supported engineering workflows, digital twins, data products and the MO360 ecosystem
Responsibility for a clearly defined work package with visible impact on the further development and adoption of eVMS
Ongoing studies in the field of business informatics, computer science, information systems, mechanical engineering, production engineering, data science or comparable studies
Strong interest in digital production planning, software products and applied artificial intelligence
Ability to understand user problems and translate them into precise, actionable software requirements
Initial experience with requirements engineering, user stories, acceptance criteria, software testing or agile development
Confidence in communicating with both technical and non-technical stakeholders
Structured, analytical and self-directed working style
Willingness to conduct user interviews, facilitate testing sessions and present software functions
Basic understanding of APIs, data models, workflow automation or software architecture is beneficial
Experience with tools such as Jira, Confluence, GitHub, Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, Microsoft Lists or n8n is an advantage
Programming or prototyping experience, for example with Python, JavaScript or REST APIs, is welcome but not mandatory
Interest in generative AI, AI agents, prompt and context engineering, MCP or knowledge graphs is a plus
Very good English skills. German skills are beneficial for interaction with local production-planning users

Supporting the design, configuration and prototype implementation of a Planning Agent with Atlassian Rovo, incl. prompt design
Developing and running test scenarios, and gathering feedback through expert reviews and user surveys
Researching current developments in LLM-based agents and AI-powered planning in agile environments (e.g. SAFe)
Documenting results and presenting them to stakeholders in the co//ab ART
Contributing to further Way of Working and toolchain topics within the team
You will get hands-on insight into a live Atlassian Jira instance used in MB.OS vehicle development and work closely with Product Managers and experts in the co//ab ART. The position is based in Sindelfingen; remote work is possible by arrangement.

Are you interested in applying modern software engineering and AI technologies to real-world challenges in automotive software development?
Mercedes-Benz AG is looking for a motivated intern to join our UI Enablers and 3D Technology group. We develop tools, technologies, and engineering solutions that support the creation of next-generation digital user experiences in Mercedes-Benz vehicles.
Our team works at the intersection of software engineering, developer tooling, automation, artificial intelligence, and 3D technology. We support an international development organization of more than 200 UI developers and continuously explore new ways to make complex development workflows more efficient, reliable, and accessible.
As an intern, you will work on practical software engineering challenges and contribute to the development of tools and technologies used by our development teams.
A particular focus will be on evaluating and applying AI-assisted engineering and agentic workflows where they provide tangible benefits. This includes building prototypes, integrating AI capabilities with existing engineering tools, and assessing their suitability for productive development environments.
You will work with technologies such as Python, GitLab, APIs, Linux, Large Language Models (LLMs) and modern AI development tools while gaining insight into software development at automotive scale.
Key Responsibilities:
Design and develop software tools and automation solutions for a large UX/UI development organization
Prototype and evaluate AI-assisted and agentic approaches for selected software engineering use cases
Develop integrations and engineering tools using Python, APIs, GitLab, and related technologies
Explore practical applications of Large Language Models and AI agents within existing development workflows
Identify opportunities to simplify repetitive or complex engineering activities through automation
Evaluate solutions with respect to quality, reliability, maintainability, and usability, not only technical feasibility
Contribute to developer tooling and engineering methods within UI Enablers and 3D Technology
Collaborate with software developers, architects, product owners, and technology experts across international teams
The activity can begin from March 2027.
Currently enrolled in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, or a comparable technical degree program
Proficiency in English and in German language
Good programming skills, preferably in Python

An analytical and structured approach to solving technical problems
Curiosity and willingness to evaluate emerging technologies critically rather than applying them for their own sake

Hands-on experience with modern software engineering, AI, automation, developer tooling, and 3D technologies
The possibility to take ideas from initial exploration through prototype and technical evaluation
Exposure to the complexity and scale of modern automotive UX/UI software development
Collaboration with experienced engineers, architects, and technology experts in an international environment
The opportunity to contribute your own technical ideas and explore emerging technologies in a professional engineering context

If you enjoy software engineering, automation, and exploring how AI can solve real technical problems, we would like to hear from you.
Join our UI Enablers and 3D Technology group and contribute to the technologies and engineering solutions behind the next generation of Mercedes-Benz digital user experiences.
